An opinion offered to guide behavior in an effort to be helpful.

examples.text: She was offered various pieces of advice on what to do.
My kids never listen to advice.
On the advice of her doctor, Mary cut down on her carbohydrates.
I have some useful advice to give you.
Sushil never took the advice of his parents, but still became rich.
We may give advice, but we can not give conduct.
Everyone always asks what my advice is, and my advice is don’t overintellectualize your art.

glosses: Deliberate consideration; knowledge.

examples.text:
How shall I dote on her with more advice,
 That thus without advice begin to love her?

glosses: Information or news given; intelligence

examples.text: late advices from France

glosses: In language about financial transactions executed by formal documents, an advisory document.

examples.text: An advice of an incoming settlement payment order may be given to an off-line receiving bank.

(g) A Reserve Bank will issue to each depositor following any transaction affecting book-entry securities maintained for such depositor under this part a confirmation thereof in the form of an advice (serially numbered or otherwise) which shall describe the amount and maturity date thereof, and include pertinent transaction data.
However, an advice of an incoming settlement payment order will be given to an off-line receiving bank only when the receiving bank has notified the Reserve Bank in writing

glosses: In commercial language, information communicated by letter; used chiefly in reference to drafts or bills of exchange

examples.text: a letter of advice
the drawees acknowledged the receipt of the letter of advice of the nineteenth of December , and promised to honor the draft when presented

glosses: A communication providing information, such as how an uncertain area of law might apply to possible future actions

examples.text: An advice issued by a Monitoring Committee could be applicable in a Dutch court

the question arises, whether an advice issued by a Monitoring Committee would actually be applicable in a Dutch court
the Executive Director will determine which requests will be referred to chief counsel for preparation of an advice and which requests will be submitted directly to the Commission for an opinion.
The central purpose of this chapter is, however, to explain how to write an advice or an opinion.

Documents and submissions to the Commission relating to a request for an opinion or an appeal of an advice shall be made at least 7 days prior to the meeting of the Commission during which the appeal or opinion will be reviewed

glosses: Counseling to perform a specific legal act.

examples.text: An honest oath taken under advice of counsel, therefore, is not perjury

glosses: Counseling to perform a specific illegal act.

An act of announcing, or giving notice.

examples.text: He raised his hand to make his announcement and said, "Excuse me everyone, I have an announcement to make."

Where else in the world can you pre-order sushi and fondue on some of the trains, travel in family carriages equipped with mini-playgrounds, or use a request stop button at some small stations? Where else can you hear the announcement: "The train at Platform 4 is ten minutes late due to an incident in another country," as I did once at the Swiss station of Spiez?

glosses: That which conveys what is announced.

examples.text: This announcement was made during the first training session.

glosses: The content which is announced.

examples.text: The announcement implied that somebody needed a spare Toshiba charger.

glosses: The act or fact of communicating anything; transmission.

examples.text: communication of smallpox
communication of a secret

glosses: The concept or state of exchanging data or information between entities.

examples.text: Some say that communication is a necessary prerequisite for sentience; others say that it is a result thereof.
The node had established communication with the network, but had as yet sent no data.

glosses: A message; the essential data transferred in an act of communication.

examples.text: Surveillance was accomplished by means of intercepting the spies' communications.

glosses: The body of all data transferred to one or both parties during an act of communication.

examples.text: The subpoena required that the company document their communication with the plaintiff.

glosses: An instance of information transfer; a conversation or discourse.

examples.text: The professors' communications consisted of lively discussions via email.
Argument […] and friendly communication.

glosses: A passageway or opening between two locations; connection.

examples.text: A round archway at the far end of the hallway provided communication to the main chamber.
The Euxine Sea is conveniently situated for trade, by the communication it has both with Asia and Europe.
This communication between the tank and pump is controlled by a float valve in the tanks and a cock in the pipe, while a poppet valve prevents the undrawn liquor going into the waste tank.

glosses: A connection between two tissues, organs, or cavities.

examples.text: ...and here a free communication had been established between the aorta and the vena cava.

glosses: Association; company.

examples.text: Evil communications corrupt good manners.

glosses: Participation in Holy Communion.

examples.text: We admit them in the Church to a right of Communication to drink of the Cup of the Bloud of Christ.

glosses: A trope by which a speaker assumes that his hearer is a partner in his sentiments, and says \"we\" instead of \"I\" or \"you\".

examples.text: Communication[…]takes place when a speaker or writer assumes his hearer or reader as a partner in his sentiments and discourse, saying We, instead of I or Ye.

glosses: A communication, or what is communicated; any concept or information conveyed.

examples.text: We've just received an urgent message from the President.
He received a message telling him to update his laptop.
I have a message from God unto thee.

No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.

glosses: An underlying theme or conclusion to be drawn from something.

examples.text: The main message of the novel is that time heals all wounds.

Even without hovering drones, a lurking assassin, a thumping score and a denouement, the real-life story of Edward Snowden, a rogue spy on the run, could be straight out of the cinema. But, as with Hollywood, the subplots and exotic locations may distract from the real message: America’s discomfort and its foes’ glee.

glosses: An errand.

examples.text: I had been on a message for my father, and was walking home along the road, when I saw a tall, fine lassie coming over the bogland on the right hand side of the road.

glosses: See messages (“groceries, shopping”).
To send a message to; to transmit a message to, e.g. as text via a cell phone.

examples.text: Just message me for directions.
I messaged her about the concert.

glosses: To send (something) as a message; usually refers to electronic messaging.

examples.text: She messaged me the information yesterday.
Please message the final report by fax.

glosses: To send a message or messages; to be capable of sending messages.

examples.text: We've implemented a new messaging service.
The runaway computer program was messaging non-stop.

glosses: To bear as a message.
The act of observing; perception.

examples.text: He took no notice of the changes, and went on as though nothing had happened.

Athelstan Arundel walked home[…], foaming and raging. […] He walked the whole way, walking through crowds, and under the noses of dray-horses, carriage-horses, and cart-horses, without taking the least notice of them.
How ready is envy to mingle with the notices which we take of other persons?

glosses: A written or printed announcement.

examples.text: Shall we post a notice about the new policy?
A notice was attached to the building reminding the residents about the five hour water shortage that was happening today.
I always read the death notices in the paper.

glosses: A formal notification or warning.

examples.text: The sidewalk adjacent to the damaged bridge stonework shall be closed until further notice.

glosses: Advance notification of termination of employment, given by an employer to an employee or vice versa.

examples.text: I gave her her mandatory two weeks' notice and sacked her.
I can't work here any longer. I'm giving notice.

glosses: A published critical review of a play or the like.

examples.text: The first-night audience, yes. The first-night reviewers, not exactly. The notices have so far been mixed, only The Financial Times having delivered itself of an unequivocal rave.

glosses: Prior notification.

examples.text: I don't mind if you want to change the venue; just give me some notice first, OK?
I have been with your father and given him notice that the Duke of Cornwall and Regan his duchess will be here with him this night.

glosses: Attention; respectful treatment; civility.
To remark upon; to mention.

examples.text: Numberless are the arguments […] that men have used morally and physically, to degrade the sex. I must notice a few.

glosses: To become aware of; to observe.

examples.text: Did you notice the flowers in her yard?
So you punched out a window for ventilation. Was that before or after you noticed you were standing in a lake of gasoline?

[The researchers] noticed many of their pieces of [plastic marine] debris sported surface pits around two microns across. Such pits are about the size of a bacterial cell. Closer examination showed that some of these pits did, indeed, contain bacteria, […].

glosses: To lavish attention upon; to treat (someone) favourably.

examples.text: She would notice her; she would improve her; she would detach her from her bad acquaintance, and introduce her into good society; she would form her opinions and her manners.

glosses: To be noticeable; to show.

examples.text: The blackness didn't notice so much when she was born; but it's unmistakeable now.

glosses: The act of notifying.
A specific piece of information that serves to notify.
A message, alert, or signal displayed by a system or application to inform the user of an event, update, new message, etc.

examples.text: A notification popped up on my computer.
I received an e-mail notification on my phone.

glosses: A statement which is proclaimed; formal public announcement.

examples.text: The Tuesday meetings are only thirty minutes now. That proclamation was made in the previous meeting.

glosses: To relate details of (an event or incident); to recount, describe (something).

examples.text: Many of these classic methods are still used, with some modern improvements. For example, with the aid of special microphones and automated sound detection software, ornithologists recently reported[…]that pine siskins (Spinus pinus) undergo an irregular, nomadic type of nocturnal migration.

glosses: To repeat (something one has heard), to retell; to pass on, convey (a message, information etc.).
To take oneself (to someone or something) for guidance or support; to appeal.

examples.text: thenne they ansuerd by and by that they coude not excuse the quene /[…]/ Allas sayd the quene I made this dyner for a good entente / and neuer for none euyl soo almyghty god me help in my ryght as I was neuer purposed to doo suche euylle dedes / and that I reporte me vnto god

glosses: To notify someone of (particular intelligence, suspicions, illegality, misconduct etc.); to make notification to relevant authorities; to submit a formal report of.

examples.text: For insurance reasons, I had to report the theft to the local police station.

glosses: To make a formal statement, especially of complaint, about (someone).

examples.text: If you do that again I'll report you to the boss.

glosses: To show up or appear at an appointed time; to present oneself.
To write news reports (for); to cover as a journalist or reporter.

examples.text: Andrew Marr reports now on more in-fighting at Westminster.
Every newspaper reported the war.
In January, the country’s weather agency sent aircraft to release chemicals into clouds over the Yellow Sea, South Korea’s Yonhap news agency reported.

glosses: To be accountable to or subordinate to (someone) in a hierarchy; to receive orders from (someone); to give official updates to (someone who is above oneself in a hierarchy).

examples.text: The financial director reports to the CEO.
Now that I've been promoted, I report to Benjamin, whom I loathe.

glosses: To return or present as the result of an examination or consideration of any matter officially referred.

examples.text: The committee reported the bill with amendments, or reported a new bill, or reported the results of an inquiry.

glosses: To take minutes of (a speech, the doings of a public body, etc.); to write down from the lips of a speaker.
To refer.

examples.text: Baldwine his ſonne, the fourth of that name [Baldwin IV of Jerusalem], ſucceeded his father [Amalric of Jerusalem]: ſo like unto him, that we report the reader to the character of King Almerick, and will ſpare the repeating his description.

glosses: To return or repeat, as sound; to echo.

examples.text: a church with windows only from above[…] that reporteth the voice twelve or thirteen times

glosses: Of a ship, to return to a port.

examples.text: Our ship leaves port on Monday and will re-port on Friday.

glosses: A piece of information describing, or an account of certain events given or presented to someone, with the most common adpositions being by (referring to creator of the report) and on (referring to the subject).

examples.text: A report by the telecommunications ministry on the phone network revealed a severe capacity problem.
Hospitals are failing to care properly for the growing number of people with dementia, according to an NHS-funded report, which has prompted demands for big improvements to help patients.

glosses: Reputation.

examples.text: I love thee in such sort / As, thou being mine, mine is thy good report.
Certain it is that if he had been daft before, he now ran wild in his pranks, and an evil report of him was in every mouth.

glosses: The sharp, loud sound from a gun or explosion.

examples.text: While their masters, the mates, seemed afraid of the sound of the hinges of their own jaws, the harpooneers chewed their food with such a relish that there was a report to it.
[…] a pistol-shot, flash and report, came from the hedge-side.

He knelt upon one knee, cocked the weapon, placed the muzzle against the man's forehead, and turning away his eyes pulled the trigger. There was no report. He had used his last cartridge for the horse.

Waziri’s warriors marched at a rapid trot through the jungle in the direction of the village. For a few minutes, the sharp cracking of guns ahead warned them to haste, but finally the reports dwindled to an occasional shot, presently ceasing altogether.

glosses: An employee whose position in a corporate hierarchy is below that of a particular manager.

examples.text: The revelation that boss of one year Laurent Freixe was conducting an undisclosed affair with a direct report has rocked a 159-year-old conglomerate that pioneered infant formula and milk chocolate before growing to become the world's largest food and beverage company.

Recomendación o consejo de cualquier tipo.
Publicación de un decreto, bando, comunicación o ley, que se hace de manera solemne para que llegue a noticia de todos.
